text.p: Italian bonds and futures ended with mild losses ahead of Wednesday's expiry of the September future, with traders saying some strength came from switching out of the outgoing contract to the December one.

Volumes on futures were fairly high and trade described as choppy and brisk. Operators were said to be buying the September future and selling December, which was 14 basis points down at 114.87. September futures fell seven basis points to 115.64.
Andrew Carless, broker at Fimat Futures in London, said the market had held up relatively well in the course of the day but nevertheless it looked toppish at current levels.
Carless cited underlying concerns about the forthcoming 1997 budget, which key economic ministers are rolling up their sleeves to address this week.

But for now the focus is on U.S. data, with the lead in the latter part of the day coming from U.S. markets following data from the National Association of Purchasing Managers, which eased worries of interest rate rises.
For Italy, the more immediate outlook also contains August final consumer prices due from Istat on Thursday, after estimates of 3.3/3.4 percent and July's actual 3.6 percent.
The lira retreated on the day, pulling back from session highs against the mark around 1,016 to 1,020 in late trade.
